LESSON: READING 7.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.2: Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How can you obtain the general idea of what a text is about?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a variety of texts for general information and enjoyment

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. read a variety of texts for general information and enjoyment
   In simple words: practise until you can read a variety of texts for general information and enjoyment. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading.
4. Show that you can: read a variety of texts for general information and enjoyment

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 7.2.1 Extensive Reading important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Learning to Learn: The learner’s ability to acquire the skill of selecting and reading a variety of texts is enhanced as they select, read and summarise texts.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you obtain the general idea of what a text is about?
2. Why is it important to read many books?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. read a variety of texts for general information and enjoyment

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
